title: How do airport luggage systems sort thousands of bags?
sources: International Air Transport Association Baggage Handling

lines.text: When you check your suitcase at an airport ticket counter, how does it navigate miles of tunnels to your plane?
lines.caps: Where does your bag go after | you *drop it at the *counter?

lines.text: It rides a subterranean roller coaster network stretching dozens of miles beneath the airport terminal.
lines.caps: Rides miles of subterranean *roller coasters | under the *terminal

lines.text: When check-in tags your bag, a ten-digit barcode containing flight, passenger, and destination data is encoded.
lines.caps: Printed barcodes encode your *flight | and passenger *identity

lines.text: High-speed optical laser tunnels scan the barcode from all six angles as the bag zooms by at thirty miles an hour.
lines.caps: 360-degree lasers scan the *tag | at thirty miles per *hour!

lines.text: Automated pusher arms kick the suitcase onto specific conveyor spurs heading toward automated explosive scanners.
lines.caps: Automated arms kick bags into *advanced | explosive *scanners

lines.text: Robotic destination loaders drop the bag into the exact cart heading for your aircraft cargo hold.
lines.caps: Robots direct luggage to your *exact | airplane cargo *bay

lines.text: Over ninety-nine percent of airport baggage arrives smoothly at its final destination.
lines.caps: Over 99% of checked *bags | arrive right on *time!
